newsitem.title: USA: Agribusiness group criticizes new U.S. CRP rules.
newsitem.headline: Agribusiness group criticizes new U.S. CRP rules.

text.p: A coalition of 124 agribusiness groups on Tuesday criticized the U.S. Agriculture Department's new rules on environmentally sensitive land.

The new Conservation Reserve Program (CRP) rules "fall far short" of making necessary changes to focus the program on conservation and the environment, the Coalition for a Competitive Food and Agriculture System said.
The group made the remarks in testimony to be submitted on Wednesday to a subcommittee of the House Agriculture Committee.

National Oilseed Processors Association executive vice president Allen Johnson, who was to testify for the coalition, said the department had used "overly broad" criteria for enrolling land in the program.
Johnson urged the department not to rush to enrol or re-enrol some 22 million acres of land that expires from the CRP on September 30.
U.S. agriculture's ability to meet growing demand while stocks were tight will depend primarily on yields and acreages, the group said.

"A CRP which protects fragile resources and yet returns good, productive acres back to production, can lead to a pro-growth agricultural economy which revitalizes rural areas and meets the growing demand for U.S. commodities," it said.

The Agriculture Department announced its new CRP rules on February 12. The program, which currently covers about 33 million acres, pays farmers to take environmentally sensitive land out of production.
